text: Late one night, Kokua took some money and went out alone, and under a street lamp she met a sick old man. <break time="0.8s" /> She told him everything and asked him to buy the bottle from Keawe for four centimes and then sell it to her for three. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man did exactly as she asked, and so the bottle came into the hands of Kokua herself. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe came home full of joy, believing that the old man now had the bottle and that he himself was free. <break time="0.8s" /> He wanted to celebrate, but Kokua could not smile, so he grew angry and went out to drink with a rough old sailor. <break time="0.8s" /> The sailor, a man who had seen much of the dark side of life, told him that a wife so sad must be hiding something. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe hurried home and saw Kokua crying over the bottle, and only then did he understand what she had done for him. <break time="0.8s" /> He gave the sailor two centimes to buy the bottle from Kokua, planning to buy it back himself for one. <break time="0.8s" /> But the sailor, who said that he was not afraid of the fire, laughed and refused to sell the bottle to anyone. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked off down the road with it, and great was the peace of Keawe and Kokua in the Bright House ever after.
